facts.claim: "Simple" by The Moth & The Flame was released as a one-track single on December 19, 2016, on Robot Farming.
"Simple" is credited as written by Andrew Tolman, Brandon Robbins and Mark Garbett, who are the band's three core members.
The lyrics are a love song. The refrain is that loving someone has "always been so simple."
The single came out less than a year after the band's major-label album Young & Unafraid (February 26, 2016, Robot Farming).
On December 20, 2016, the day after the single's release, singer Brandon Robbins had a kidney transplant from longtime friend Corey Fox. The band went on hiatus while they recovered.
The band formed in Provo, Utah, in 2011. Its members are singer/guitarist Brandon Robbins, keyboardist Mark Garbett and drummer Andrew Tolman, who was previously Imagine Dragons' drummer.
The band is now based in Los Angeles. Its labels have included Hidden Records, Elektra Records and Robot Farming.
Young & Unafraid was produced by Peter Katis, Tony Hoffer and Nate Pyfer, with string arrangements by Rob Moose. Nothing found credits any of them on "Simple."
The band's follow-up album Ruthless came out February 1, 2019, via Robot Farming/Thirty Tigers. It dealt with mental health themes, and Robbins has spoken openly about his depression.

research.lineage: The band is an alternative/art-rock group that came out of the Provo, Utah scene alongside Imagine Dragons, and later moved to Los Angeles.

draft:
The strangest line in **Simple** is the one that sounds like comfort. "There is no way you can understand," Brandon Robbins sings, and then he offers love as a guide anyway, and a promise that things will work out in the end. It's a love song built on a contradiction it never tries to fix. The narrator insists everything has "always been so simple" while telling the other person they couldn't possibly follow it. That's how certainty sounds when it's trying to calm someone else's doubt. The singer is sure, but the reassurance gives away that somebody in this room isn't.

The opening sets that up. The world says to wait and see, and the narrator answers, "But I've known since the day I fell." There's pride in that line, a quiet flex of conviction. But the song keeps circling back to persuasion, which suggests the certainty still needs defending. Then the second verse does something small and telling: the invitation to be led by love breaks off at "Let love take you by," and the hand never arrives. Whether you hear that as a stumble or as the moment words stop being enough, the gap matters.

The sound leans toward warmth over drama. A clean electric guitar plays shimmering, sustained arpeggios. Bass holds long root notes underneath, and the drums keep a soft, simple kick-snare-cymbal pulse at a slow, rolling ballad tempo. Robbins' voice is breathy and a little strained, as if the plainness of the lyric costs him something to say out loud. A higher harmony voice joins him and fills in the space. The arrangement builds gradually, one layer at a time, in a polished, roomy mix that leaves plenty of air around everything.

The band came out of the Provo, Utah scene in 2011, alongside Imagine Dragons. Drummer Andrew Tolman played in that band before this one. Tolman, Robbins and keyboardist Mark Garbett share the writing credit. **Simple** shows how restrained a group from that arena-leaning scene can be. Nothing swells into a chant. The single arrived on Robot Farming on December 19, 2016, less than a year after *Young & Unafraid*. The next day, Robbins had a kidney transplant from his longtime friend Corey Fox, and the band went on hiatus while they recovered. The lyric never mentions any of that. It just keeps repeating that things will work out.

The song holds out its steadiness like a hand, and you feel how much the person offering it needs you to take it.
